name: Another Text Editor (ATE)
subtitle: Text, code and local projects
promotionalText: Write text, edit code and organize local projects with readable text, document tabs and offline syntax checks. No account or advertising.
description:
Another Text Editor (ATE) gives you a clear space to write text, edit source files and organize local projects on iPhone, iPad and Mac.

WRITE COMFORTABLY
Choose readable document text from 10 to 54 points, light or dark appearance, and text or icon buttons. Use Basic mode for everyday writing and Advanced mode for coding tools.

KEEP FILES ORGANIZED
Work with up to 12 document tabs. Create projects, folders and text files, add existing files to the selected folder, and transfer saved project files using ZIP import and export. Exact filenames are preserved, including names without an extension.

EDIT WITH FAMILIAR TOOLS
Syntax colors, automatic indentation, search and replace, Go to line, undo and redo, selection and copy are included. Optional Vim key bindings work best with a hardware keyboard.

CHECK SYNTAX OFFLINE
Bundled checks cover JavaScript, TypeScript syntax, JSON, YAML, HTML, CSS, Python syntax, sh/Bash structure, SQLite SQL and basic C structure. Markdown includes selected lint warnings. Tap an issue to jump to its location. Checks do not execute your code, validate all program behavior or replace a compiler or IDE.

LOCAL BY DESIGN
No account, advertising or advertising tracking. Documents and recovery stay on your device unless you choose a file provider or sharing destination. Save independent file copies: local recovery is not a backup or cross-device synchronization.

On iPhone and iPad, Save file uses the share sheet: choose Save to Files and complete the save. On Mac, use the native Save dialog. Full guides, support and privacy information are available from Help.

ATE is free, with no subscriptions or in-app purchases.

review.notes:
No account, login, subscription, purchase or review credentials are required. On first launch read Terms of Use, tick I have read and agree, then Accept and continue. Menu > Help reopens terms and links Privacy, Support and both guides.

Basic is the default. Write a note and Save file. iPhone/iPad: choose Save to Files in the system share sheet and complete the save. Mac: use the native Save dialog. Cancelling keeps the draft. Menu > Advanced enables syntax tools, Vim and Projects. Open project > New project creates a workspace; choose a folder then Add file > Create file or Choose files. Tap a file in the tree to open it. Close project keeps saved files. Delete folder previews contents and refuses unsaved affected tabs and project root.

For a bundled syntax demonstration, create demo.sql, enter SELECT FROM;, then Check syntax. Correct to SELECT 1; and check again. SQL is SQLite grammar; there is no database. Python checks syntax without executing imports or code. The App Store Mac edition uses offline Basic C and hides external compiler configuration. All parsers and Wasm assets are bundled for offline use.

ATE is a local general-purpose text editor with no hosted public content, messaging, browsing feed or program execution. External navigation is limited to user-requested help/legal/support pages. Developer does not collect document contents or app analytics. Website hosts may receive ordinary web requests. There are no regional feature differences.

Review contact phone is maintained privately in App Store Connect, not in this repository.
